name.text: Relations Q7 - Which equation is one-to-many

questiontext.text: Which of the following equations represents a one-to-many relation?

generalfeedback.text:
Check each equation by asking whether a single input value of x can give more than one value of y.

For y = 3x minus 5, each x gives exactly one y, so this is one-to-one.

For y = x cubed, each x also gives exactly one y, and different x values give different y values, so this is one-to-one too.

For y equals the absolute value of x, each x gives one y, though different x values, such as 2 and negative 2, give the same y. This makes it many-to-one, not one-to-many.

Now check x squared plus y squared equals 9. This is the equation of a circle. Rearranging for y, we get two possible values for almost every x between negative 3 and 3, the positive square root of 9 minus x squared, and the negative square root of 9 minus x squared. So one input value of x gives two output values of y. This matches a one-to-many relation. The correct answer is B.

prtcorrect.text: Correct. Read the worked solution below to confirm your reasoning.

prtpartiallycorrect.text: Not quite. Read the worked solution below.

prtincorrect.text: Not correct. Read the worked solution below.
